heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro give creative teams precision, speed, and control for professional image and video generation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected editorial-labs hero: full-width dark navy canvas with a strong left-anchored headline block and a right-side layered media shell embedded into the background rather than a simple split. Build the hero around premium abstract product UI cards, frame sequences, and waveform motifs instead of photography. Keep the orange CTA as the dominant focal point, add subtle grid lines and gradient meshes for technical credibility, and maintain generous negative space so the long value proposition reads cleanly. This should feel enterprise-grade, proof-led, and designed for creative professionals.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split hero for continuity with the ad message, but make the right side an abstract product shell instead of a standard promo image.
Use a static logo trust band immediately after the hero because trustStrategy is logos-first and traffic is warm.
Make the product story alternate between a tabs-with-preview experience for Seedream 4.5 and a split-panel narrative for Seedance 1.5 Pro so adjacent sections feel different.
Shift from product explanation into testimonial spotlight cards to avoid a monotonous feature grid rhythm.
Finish with a high-contrast pricing/cart-style conversion block rather than a generic footer CTA.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore multimodal image generation, synchronized audio-video creation, and enterprise-ready creative control.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark navy base with layered translucent panels, subtle grid noise, and orange edge glow around the media shell
sections.designNote: Hero must be content-first and answer the 3 hero checks clearly: what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the headline direct: AI image and video generation for creative teams. Use a compact benefit stack under the subheadline, then a single primary button labeled Get started in accent orange at full opacity. The right side should show a premium abstract interface with image tiles, frame strips, and audio-wave cues, not people or generic marketing art. This section should feel dynamic and immediately relevant to warm traffic.

Place a prominent logo-first trust band directly below the hero. Since actual logos are not provided, use a clean 3-6 item recognisable logo grid only if real logos are available; otherwise fall back to a restrained metrics strip. Keep it short and proof-heavy, with minimal copy and no decorative card clutter.

This section should open with Seedream 4.5 as the primary click-driver because the audience is visually creative and the model has five features, requiring tabs or an interactive spotlight rather than a static grid. Present the image-generation capabilities in a left-side tab stack with a preview panel showing resolution, typography, composition, and editing examples. Then shift to Seedance 1.5 Pro in a contrasting split-panel block below or beside it, using a more cinematic visual language and audio-video synchronization cues. Do not use identical card structures for both products. Seedream gets the deeper interactive focus; Seedance gets a more narrative, motion-led treatment.

Use a proof-led visual rhythm here with testimonial spotlight cards and a supporting quote grid. Because the available proof is testimonial-based rather than logo-rich, keep the strongest 2-3 quotes visually dominant and let the remaining quotes sit in smaller supporting cards. Emphasize benefits like speed, precision, and creative control. This should feel editorial and credible, not like a generic review carousel.

After proof, reinforce the two click-driving features with a dense but restrained split-panel feature treatment. Keep Seedream and Seedance separated by visual language: one panel for image generation precision and one for video motion and synchronization. Use a strong left/right contrast, with one side text-dominant and the other side image-dominant. Do not repeat the same layout from the product section; this block should feel more distilled and executive.

Present pricing as a compact two-option comparison with one highlighted path, not a multi-plan SaaS table. Keep the card treatment premium and conversion-oriented. Use a strong orange accent on the primary path, and repeat only the required CTA button label Get started in the checkout action area. Make this section feel like a decision point, not a catalog.

Use a 3-card testimonial grid with concise quotes from creative roles. This should be more compact than the proof section and act as reinforcement rather than the main trust driver. Keep the cards uniform but avoid the same visual pattern as the previous proof block by using a tighter grid with reduced text density.

End with a focused floating lead card or quote/demo capture card, but keep the CTA label locked to Get started. Since warm traffic already saw the hero CTA, this final block should be clean and decisive rather than aggressive. Make the form area feel like the simplest next step for a creative team evaluating the product.
Low-priority utility footer only. Keep it visually quiet so the preceding conversion section remains dominant.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is long and needs to stay strong without breaking into awkward multi-line stacking. 48px preserves impact while keeping the layout controlled on a dark, proof-heavy landing page.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen top hero with brand/logo at upper left, strong H1, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list beneath. Uses a broad full-width banner feel with left-aligned content and a distinct visual hierarchy rather than a centered marketing splash.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero first, then a lead-generation/form block, followed by feature/product explanation blocks. Rhythm is linear and stacked, with each section serving a single purpose and minimal lateral complexity.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Solid white content cards with simple borders or subtle elevation, rounded or soft-cornered container treatment, and dense informational content. Cards prioritize readability and form handling over decorative styling.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is placed prominently in the hero and repeated in section-level feature blocks. CTA treatment is direct and conversion-oriented, with a strong verb-led label and minimal secondary-action noise.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing system in the reference pattern. If added, pricing should follow the same compact card-based treatment used for content blocks, with clear hierarchy and a single dominant plan emphasis.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided reference; implied pattern is a standard utility footer after stacked content, with low visual priority compared to hero and lead form sections.
spacingScale: tight inner spacing within lists and form fields
moderate spacing between headline, paragraph, and CTAs
large vertical separation between major sections
compact bullet/item spacing for feature readability
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Media is secondary to copy and form capture. The reference favors logo/brand placement and content-led panels over large hero imagery, video embeds, or gallery-style media.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Each product section should use a label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and a structured feature list. Feature lists are best rendered as stacked rows or compact cards with clear title/description pairing, supporting progressive disclosure of capabilities.
referenceMap.formPattern: A dedicated lead form block sits directly after the hero, visually separated as a conversion module. The form uses a card container, heading, multiple input fields, and hidden tracking fields, indicating a friction-light capture pattern with analytics integration.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Minimal-motion, mostly static presentation with no strong evidence of animated reveals or motion-driven storytelling. Any motion should be restrained and functional, such as basic slider behavior if introduced.
componentPatterns: section headings with short descriptive copy
designNotes: Optimize for B2B conversion and information density.
Keep hierarchy clear: logo, headline, support copy, benefits, CTA, then form.
Use stacked layouts over complex multi-column storytelling.
Introduce product capabilities through labeled sections and compact feature rows.
Prefer utility over decoration; the pattern is functional and lead-oriented.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for solution-aware professionals evaluating advanced AI image and video tools, so the strategy should move quickly from promise to proof to inquiry. Because the instruction says visitors trust logos most, the strongest trust treatment should be a logo-first strip near the hero, supported by concise testimonials later. The content is already long and technical, which fits a dense product-led layout with stacked sections and clear separation between Seedream and Seedance. A split hero is best for a dark-theme B2B page because it can carry a sharp message on one side and a relevant product/human visual on the other without needing extra lead magnets. CTA intensity should be strong, with direct demo/quote actions repeated across sections to support lead capture.
